subject: Agriculture
title: Land Subsidence
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Land Subsidence.

hook.text: Pump too much groundwater and the ground above literally sinks. Parts of California have dropped 28 feet.

buildup.text: When water is removed from pore spaces, clay layers compact permanently. The ground can never rise back.

discovery.text: Subsidence cracks foundations, breaks pipelines, and damages canals—infrastructure built on stable ground that isn't.

twist.text: It's irreversible. Once the aquifer compacts, it can never hold as much water again—storage lost forever.

climax.text: Mexico City, Jakarta, and the San Joaquin Valley are all sinking from groundwater extraction.

punchline.text: Drain the water, sink the city. No refund.

quiz.question: Why is land subsidence from groundwater pumping irreversible?
options: The water is too deep to replace
Compacted clay layers can never re-expand to their original size
